subject: Re: Order Form — temporary suspension of minimums and Q4 true-up waiver
messages:
From: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary suspension of minimum commit / Q4 true-up waiver (Order Form v3 redline)

Evelyn —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As we prepare to finalize Order Form v3, procurement has pushed back on the Minimum Annual Commitment and the Q4 true-up mechanics in Exhibit B/C. Seasonality for BrightCart is unusual (holiday prep and vendor consolidation) and the procurement team is asking if Redwood will accept a temporary suspension of the MAC true-up for Q4 or, alternatively, a one-time holdback/credit in lieu of the true-up.

I’ve attached our redline to the order form with comments on Exhibit B Section 2 (minimums), Exhibit C (true-up window and calculation), and an ask to soften the floor for the first 12 months. Their asks:
- Suspend enforcement of the Q4 true-up for the 2026 contract year (i.e., no invoice true-up for Oct-Dec).
- If suspension is not possible, allow a one-time credit equal to 25% of the outstanding true-up calculation.
- Allow a 60-day invoice grace period for any net true-up amounts.

Can Redwood legal and finance take a look and advise which of these options are feasible? Procurement is hoping to have a signed amendment by next Tuesday.

Attached: BrightCart_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

—Tim Sullivan
Procurement Lead, BrightCart
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@brightcart.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary suspension of minimum commit / Q4 true-up waiver (Order Form v3 redline)

Tim —

Appreciate the context and the redline. We want to be pragmatic here and keep the deal moving. I’ve looped in Legal (Monica) and Finance (Marcus) to evaluate the risk and cashflow impact. Initial thoughts from Sales: we can likely offer a temporary accommodation tied to the following constraints (happy to put in legal language if that helps):

- Option A (preferred): Waive the Q4 true-up for the 2026 contract year only; include an explicit clause that the waiver is a one-time concession and does not change the calculation methodology for future years.
- Option B (fallback): Apply a one-time credit equal to 15%–25% of the computed true-up, with the exact percentage to be confirmed by Finance.
- Both options should be accompanied by a 60-day invoice grace period and a revised invoice schedule (no retroactive term changes to the MAC beyond this amendment).

Ask to Legal: can you draft short amendment language for Option A and Option B and flag any compliance/audit concerns (e.g., does this trigger audit rights or change how we report revenue recognition for Redwood)?

Marcus — can you run a quick impact calc for both options so we can present numbers to BrightCart? Monica — if you can push back a redline that keeps our termination and SLA exposure limited that would be ideal.

I’ll hold next Tuesday afternoon open for a quick signature push if we can get legal/finance sign-off by Monday EOD.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary suspension of minimum commit / Q4 true-up waiver (Order Form v3 redline)

Team —

Reviewed BrightCart's redline and Evelyn’s proposed options. High-level reactions and clarifying Qs below:

1) Revenue recognition / audit implications: A one-time waiver will reduce recognized revenue for the period where the true-up would have applied. If Finance confirms the expected delta is immaterial we can proceed; otherwise we need explicit accounting language in the amendment acknowledging the waiver and the period it affects. This protects both parties for external audit.

2) Term / renewal mechanics: Any waiver must be explicitly timeboxed to "Contract Year 2026" and include language that the underlying MAC, caps, and floors revert to the baseline calculation method thereafter. Do not change the renewal trigger or the MAC baseline.

3) SLA and termination exposure: We should not accept any language that increases our SLA or termination exposure. Proposed redline: insert new Exhibit amendment clause: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Parties agree that the true-up obligation for Contract Year 2026 is waived in whole, and such waiver is a one-time concession and does not modify any other obligations under the Agreement."

4) Audit & access: If we waive the true-up, we should retain the standard audit right for a 12-month lookback to validate usage but waive any collection action during the 2026 Q4 suspension period. Suggested wording: "Customer audit rights remain unchanged; however, Redwood will not invoice or seek collection on any amounts arising solely from the Contract Year 2026 true-up during the suspension period."

5) Clean fallback language for Option B (credit): If we go credit route, propose a formula and cap: "Customer shall receive a one-time credit equal to X% of the calculated true-up for Contract Year 2026, not to exceed $[cap]. The credit will be applied to the first invoice following execution of this Amendment." Need Finance to supply X and cap.

I can draft two short amendment snippets (Option A and Option B) — attach as a Word doc for negotiation. Also want to confirm: do we require an authorized signature from procurement (line-item), or will Tim accept a countersignature via DocuSign once we circulate an amendment? Knowing this will speed a turnaround.

Drafts attached: BrightCart_ExhibitB_Proposed_Amendment.docx

—Monica
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary suspension of minimum commit / Q4 true-up waiver (Order Form v3 redline)

Evelyn / Monica —

Ran the numbers against the deal entry (BRTC-2026-Q4-47). Quick summary of financial impact (approximate):

- Full waiver (Option A): Revenue deferral of ~$420k for 2026 (amount that would have been collected Oct–Dec true-up). P&L impact is a deferral; cash impact = $0 immediate collection for Q4 items.
- 15% credit (lower bound fallback): immediate revenue impact ~$63k; net cash collected on true-up increases by 85% of the calculated amount.
- 25% credit (upper bound asked by customer): immediate revenue impact ~$105k.

Recommended commercial route: Offer Option A (full suspension) only if BrightCart signs a short amendment that: (a) explicitly states the waiver is one-time and timeboxed to 2026, (b) preserves audit rights but defers collection until Q1 2027 if an audit finds additional usage, and (c) includes a $50k cap on any subsequent true-up collection for administrative simplicity. If customer declines Option A, offer a 20% credit as compromise.

Also note cash forecasting: if we accept Option A we should set aside the $420k as a receivable risk in next month’s forecast for revenue ops.

I’ll prepare the numeric callouts (spreadsheet) if you want to include them in the attachment for BrightCart — otherwise the amendment can reference the true-up calculation method and leave numeric items to invoice post-signature.

—Marcus
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary suspension of minimum commit / Q4 true-up waiver (Order Form v3 redline)

Tim —

Thanks for the redline and for explaining procurement's needs. We’ve discussed internally and can proceed with Option A (one-time suspension) under limited conditions:

1) The waiver applies only to Contract Year 2026 and expressly reverts all MAC, cap/floor, and true-up calculation mechanics to the baseline for subsequent years.
2) Redwood retains standard audit rights; Redwood will not invoice or pursue collection for amounts arising solely from the Contract Year 2026 true-up during the suspension period. If an audit after Jan 1, 2027 identifies underreported usage for 2026, Redwood may pursue collection up to a $50,000 cap.
3) The waiver is effective only upon execution of a signed Amendment to the Order Form. We will circulate a two-line amendment via DocuSign for signature (no other terms changed).

I’ve attached the proposed amendment language as a Doc (and included the redline you sent). If that looks acceptable, please confirm by EOD Tuesday and we’ll send the DocuSign link. If procurement prefers a credit instead, we can offer a 20% one-time true-up credit as a fallback.

Attached: DocuSign_BRTC_OrderForm_Amendment_link.txt (DocuSign link will be live after legal populates the amendment)

Next steps: Monica will upload the legal amendment; Marcus is prepped to confirm the exact cap and accounting notes; if BrightCart confirms Option A we’ll route for signatures and aim to finalize by Wednesday.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
